name: Chinese Dream
summary: The Chinese Dream is Xi Jinping's formula for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, presented as the long-held goal of recovering national strength after the century of humiliation. Officially it has three parts, a prosperous and strong country, national rejuvenation and people's happiness, and it is tied to socialism with Chinese characteristics, to leadership by the Communist Party and to targets for 2021 and 2049. Scholars describe it as the signature slogan of Xi's era, deliberately broad, serving national pride and the Party's legitimacy.
scope: The Dream as set out in Xi Jinping's 2012 Road to Rejuvenation speech and in the 19th and 20th Party Congress reports that name it, as read by the scholarship that defines the term (Hitkari, Kaminski). It covers the official formulation of national rejuvenation; the wider programme of Xi Jinping Thought, the Party's ideology in general and Chinese nationalism are separate subjects, and a Congress-report passage counts here only where it is presented as part of the path to the Dream.

notes: Words only: the sources are Xi's speech and two Congress reports, so every answer is stated doctrine and no record sources (the PRC's practice) were tagged as actions; answers where practice might point elsewhere (media, surveillance, elections, religion's treatment) were left null or kept to what the reports state. Themes searched in the reports: Party leadership, army, economy and ownership, welfare and health, population, energy and climate, culture and education, religion, ethnic affairs, Taiwan, Hong Kong, foreign policy and alliances, intellectual property, rule of law, democracy. Wikipedia's page was used only to find leads. Britannica and the Davey thesis (core.ac.uk) refused scripted access and were not used.
